claims.text: Combining metadynamics or thermodynamic integration with HEA-specific interatomic potentials can accurately and efficiently determine HEA melting temperatures.
The integrated method can determine HEA enthalpies of fusion.
The integrated method can determine HEA entropies of fusion.
The integrated method can determine HEA volume changes at melting.
The integrated method can determine liquid-phase thermodynamic properties and free-energy profiles for HEAs.
The proposed performance applies across broad HEA compositional space.
HEAs across the proposed compositional range initially form disordered solid solutions below their melting points.
Free-energy valleys sampled by the method correspond to solid and liquid states and include features of the solid-liquid interface transition state.
Enhanced sampling overcomes kinetic trapping during simulation of HEA melting.
Enhanced sampling overcomes finite-size limitations during simulation of HEA melting.
Reconstructing the free-energy landscape at adequate resolution identifies solid-liquid phase-coexistence conditions.
The reconstructed coexistence landscape provides detailed estimates of latent heat, entropy change, and volume difference at melting.
Predicted melting temperature, fusion enthalpy, fusion entropy, and melting volume change will be within approximately 5% of high-precision experimental or first-principles benchmarks.
The method will generate a reliable liquid-phase free-energy profile for HEAs.
Traditional calorimetric techniques such as DSC are limited by experimental inefficiency for the proposed HEA-wide task.
Conventional molecular dynamics provides insufficient free-energy sampling in complex HEAs.
The approach is most applicable to HEAs for which reliable interatomic potentials exist.
Extreme compositions or systems with interactions not represented by available potentials require additional calibration or alternative methods.
Quantitative performance depends on interatomic-potential quality and sampling efficiency.
Deviation of any benchmarked melting quantity by more than approximately 5%, or failure to reproduce phase coexistence, is designated as a result that falsifies the approach.
